d: Luau is the scripting language creators use in Roblox Studio.
h:
Luau is the scripting language creators use in Roblox Studio. It is a fast, small, safe, gradually typed embeddable scripting language derived from Lua 5.1.

Contributing your Luau scripts for AI training can help enhance Luau-focused AI tools in Studio. For more information, see Empower Luau creation.

Support in Studio

The Script Editor in Studio supports Luau with autocompletion, syntax highlighting, static linting, type checking, and script analysis. It also shows documentation and function signatures for members of the Roblox Engine API.

Types

Luau includes the following data types:

  • Nil represents non-existence or nothingness. It's different from any other value or data type.
  • Booleans, or bool, have a value of either false or true.
  • Numbers, or double, represent double-precision (64-bit) floating-point numbers.
  • Strings are sequences of characters, such as letters, numbers, and symbols.
  • Tables are arrays or dictionaries of any value except nil.
  • Enums are fixed lists of items.

Luau is dynamically typed by default. Variables, function parameters, and return values can be any data type. This helps you write code faster because you don't need to provide types for each piece of data. You can still declare explicit types for variables in Luau and enable strict type checking to make type issues obvious and easy to locate.

Data structures

You can also implement the following data structures using primitive data types:

  • Stacks are Last-In-First-Out collections of items that you can implement using tables.
  • Queues are First-In-First-Out collections of items that you can implement using tables.
  • Metatables are tables with advanced configurations that can achieve functionalities such as storing pairs of keys and values and calculating arithmetic operations.

Features

In Luau, variables and functions can have global and local scope within a script. Luau has logical, relational, and compound assignment operators. You can use control structures and functions to control when Luau executes code. Many operators and variable assignments perform type coercion to change values to the types that Luau expects.

kid.simple: Luau is the language you write scripts in when you make games in Roblox Studio. It is based on an older language called Lua, but it is faster and safer. This page is a map of the Luau basics: the kinds of values you can use, a few handy ways to organize data, and the main features like variables, functions, and if statements. Start here to see what to learn next.
kid.analogy: Luau is like the language your game understands. Data types are the kinds of words (names, numbers, yes/no answers), and features like functions and if statements are the grammar that lets you make full sentences.
keyPoints: Luau is Roblox's scripting language, built from Lua 5.1.
The Script Editor in Studio helps you with autocomplete, color highlighting, and warnings about mistakes.
Main data types: `nil` (nothing), booleans (`true`/`false`), numbers, strings (text), tables (lists and dictionaries), and enums (fixed lists of choices).
Luau is dynamically typed: a variable can hold any kind of value, so you do not have to label types.
You can still add type labels and turn on strict type checking to catch mistakes early.
Using tables, you can build stacks (last in, first out), queues (first in, first out), and metatables (tables with special powers).
Other key features: variables, scope, operators, control structures like `if` and loops, functions, and type coercion.

terms.scripting language: A language for writing instructions (scripts) that tell your game what to do.
terms.data type: The kind of value something is, like a number (5), a string ("hi"), or a boolean (true).
terms.dynamically typed: A variable can hold any type and even switch types. `x = 5` then `x = "hi"` is allowed.
terms.gradually typed: You can add type labels to some of your code and leave the rest without them.
terms.type checking: Studio looking over your code to warn you when you use the wrong kind of value.
terms.linting: Automatic checks that point out likely mistakes while you type.
terms.autocompletion: Studio suggesting the rest of a word or name as you type.
terms.data structure: A way to organize lots of values, like a list or a stack.
terms.embeddable: Built to live inside a bigger program, like how Luau runs inside Roblox.

example.title: Try each basic data type
example.code:
-- nil means nothing
local nothing = nil
-- booleans are true or false
local isGameOver = false
-- numbers can be whole or have decimals
local coins = 25
-- strings are text
local playerName = "Builder"
-- tables hold many values
local inventory = { "Sword", "Shield" }
-- enums are fixed lists of choices
local shape = Enum.PartType.Ball

print(nothing, isGameOver, coins, playerName, inventory[1], shape)
-- Output: nil false 25 Builder Sword Enum.PartType.Ball
explain: Each `local` line makes a variable holding a different type of value.
`inventory[1]` gets the first item in the table, "Sword".
`print` shows all of them in the Output window.

watchOut: Expecting Luau to work exactly like other languages. For example, in Luau 0 and the empty string count as true.
Ignoring the Script Editor's underlines. They often point to real bugs; hover to read the warning.
